lean.fidelity_note: The paper and the formal statement both assert that one solution satisfying Theorem 1.1 can be chosen with a smooth space-time extension through $T_*$ away from the torus origin. Thus the same solution has bounded velocity, divergent gradient and vorticity integrals, central vorticity divergence and the two off-origin spatial limits. The formal statement also records uniqueness of its maximal velocity and lifespan. The extension is periodic; it is not required to solve Euler after $T_*$. The proof uses an auxiliary theorem that selects an exponent and threshold and produces an extension smooth away from the integer lattice for all real times. This stronger input suffices for the local existential remark. It does not establish the auxiliary note’s broader assertion for every threshold satisfying its additional estimates; the supplied auxiliary statement file explicitly leaves that broader assertion outside the proved sequence of numbered results.

statements.markdown: **Remark 1.2.** The solution in Theorem 1.1 may be chosen so that it extends smoothly in space and time through $T_*$ away from the origin. A proof is given in the auxiliary note \[[31](#cite-TerminalSmoothness)\].
